title: Streamlined Sales Tax Governing Board: Remote Seller State Guidance (state thresholds and compliance dates)

history.reason: Source read directly on the access date; findings transcribed from the document.

publisher: Streamlined Sales Tax Governing Board, Inc. (interstate state-government organization)
reliability: Published by an organization of member states that administers the Streamlined program and promotes simplification and CSP use; states are the parties imposing the obligation. The page says it is general guidance, not legal advice, and does not override state law.
findings: The page states the chart summarizes remote-seller thresholds and compliance dates "as of January 11, 2023", yet the text also contains later entries (for example Illinois effective 1/1/2026, Utah effective 7/1/2025, Alaska effective 1/1/2025); it is therefore a mix of dates and was read on 2026-11-04.
By my count of the extracted text, 47 of 52 rows (46 states plus the District of Columbia) show a dollar threshold; Delaware (no sales tax), Montana, New Hampshire, Oregon and Puerto Rico show none.

Most thresholds are $100,000 of sales, many historically or currently "or 200 transactions"; Alabama and Mississippi list $250,000; California and Texas list $500,000; New York lists $500,000 and more than 100 sales.

Thresholds are measured differently across states: sales vs. transactions (OR vs. AND), gross sales, gross revenue, retail sales or taxable sales; many states do not distinguish taxable from non-taxable sales; period (previous or current calendar year, preceding 12 months) varies.
Several states changed thresholds over time (for example removing the 200-transaction test in Indiana, North Carolina, Wyoming, Alaska, Wisconsin, North Dakota).
A seller with physical presence in a state must register regardless of sales amount; economic nexus applies to sellers without it.
limitations: No publication date is shown for the whole page; the chart is self-dated January 11, 2023 but contains later edits, so accuracy of every row is unverified.
Row counts are my tally of extracted text and were not cross-checked with state revenue department sites.
Does not give rates, filing frequency, local-tax rules or marketplace-facilitator details; does not measure compliance cost.
